verdict.summary: Connecting your own Xero organisation is quick: register an app, paste the credentials into Composio, and authorise. Reaching other customers is the hard part, because certification, an annual security assessment and, for some tiers, an App Store listing are required, and Xero publishes no review timeline.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 30-60 min for your own connection; 1-2 days of forms and assessment prep for broader distribution, plus unpublished review time
verdict.time_to_first_connection: About 15-30 min after you have a Xero login and a Xero organisation to connect
verdict.approval_wait: None for connecting your own organisation. Certification, security assessment and App Store listing have no published timeline; one third-party source reports several months for the financial-services path.

gates.name: New app, own organisation (Starter plan)
gates.unlocks: Create the app and connect your own Xero organisation through Composio. No review.
limits: New apps start on the free Starter plan (5 connections maximum).
Starter-tier apps get 1,000 API calls per day per organisation.
Access tokens last 30 minutes; refresh tokens expire after 60 days if unused.
The client secret is shown only once at generation.

gates.name: Uncertified app, limited connections (Starter and Core)
gates.unlocks: Connect a small number of other organisations to the uncertified app. Starter and Core have no certification prerequisite.
limits: Each Xero organisation can connect at most 5 uncertified apps; certified apps have no such limit.
Starter caps at 5 connections; Core caps at 50 (AUD 35 per month).
A sixth connection requires adding payment details, which moves the app to Core.
A third-party source says users can install at most 2 uncertified apps; not confirmed on Xero's pages.
Rate limits are the same for all apps and cannot be raised on request: 5 concurrent calls, 60 per minute, 5,000 per day per connection, and 10,000 calls per minute app-wide.
gates.time_to_reach: Minutes after Gate 1, once you choose to connect more organisations; a sixth connection needs payment details added.

gates.name: Certified and listed app (Plus tier and above)
gates.unlocks: Wide distribution: certified apps have no per-organisation uncertified-app limit, and listing in the Xero App Store is possible.
limits: App certification is a prerequisite from the Plus tier up (Plus AUD 245 per month; Advanced AUD 1,445 per month).
All app partners must pass a Xero security assessment, repeated annually.
Partners at 1,000 or more connections must also pass an advanced security assessment.
App Store listing is required for Enterprise, optional for Plus and Advanced, and not available for Starter or Core.
Journals endpoint, Xero Practice Manager API and Bulk Connections need security assessment and use-case approval, Advanced tier only.
gates.time_to_reach: Not published by Xero; certification and security assessment must pass first.

steps.title: Sign in to the Xero Developer portal
steps.detail: Open My Apps at the developer portal and sign in with the Xero account you will use to manage the app. The page is JavaScript-only, so enable JavaScript or it will not load.
gotchas: Your Xero login must be a developer account; the page itself has no login wall but the app creation flow requires sign-in.

steps.title: Create a new app
steps.detail: Choose New app at the top right. Pick an integration type; the findings do not confirm whether web or mobile/desktop changes redirect URI rules, so choose web app unless Composio specifies otherwise. Enter the company or application URL.
gotchas: Xero's documentation does not state whether integration type changes redirect URI rules; third-party guides use both.

steps.title: Register the Composio redirect URI
steps.detail: In the redirect URI field, paste the exact callback URL shown in your Composio auth config for Xero. Xero requires absolute URIs with no wildcards, and allows up to 50 per app. Register only the URL Composio shows.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Wildcards are not supported; a mismatch causes the authorisation to fail.
Composio's default callback has been https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add in the research; confirm it against your auth config.

steps.title: Accept the terms and create the app
steps.detail: Read the Xero Developer Platform Terms & Conditions, tick to agree, and click Create app. Note that the terms prohibit using Xero API data to train AI or machine-learning models.
gotchas: The AI/ML training prohibition applies to new developers from 4 December 2025 and to existing developers from 2 March 2026.

steps.title: Generate and save the client secret
steps.detail: On the app's configuration page, generate a client secret. Copy the client ID and the client secret into a password manager immediately, because the secret is viewable only once. If you lose it, generate a new one.

values.label: Client ID
values.value: Shown on the app configuration page

values.label: Client secret
values.value: Generated once on the app configuration page

gotchas: The secret cannot be viewed again after it is first shown.

steps.title: Enter the credentials in Composio
steps.detail: In the Composio Xero auth config, paste the client ID and client secret from the previous step. Composio has no managed Xero OAuth, so this step is required before any connection works.

steps.title: Review the scope list
steps.detail: Check the requested scopes. New apps created on or after 2 March 2026 can only use granular scopes, so Composio's default granular list should work. Include offline_access so Composio receives a refresh token. Drop scopes you do not need: Scopes are additive on re-authorisation, so earlier grants stay even if you later request fewer.
gotchas: Journals, Payroll and Practice Manager scopes are not in Composio's default list. Payroll requires the connecting user to be a Payroll Admin.
Reports scopes need the connecting user to hold Reports access.

steps.title: Connect your own organisation as a test
steps.detail: From Composio, start the Xero connection with your own Xero login and select one organisation. Confirm the connection appears as active. This completes Gate 1.
gotchas: A connection is counted per user and organisation pair, and it counts toward the Starter cap of 5.
Access tokens expire after 30 minutes; Composio must refresh them, and a refresh token unused for 60 days expires.

steps.title: Draft compliance text for review
steps.detail: Draft the scope justification, data-use statement and an AI/ML training statement that states the app does not use Xero API data to train models. Use these as the basis for the security assessment and listing later.

steps.title: Move to a paid tier if you need more than 5 connections
steps.detail: Add payment details in the developer portal before adding a sixth connection. This moves the app from Starter to Core (AUD 35 per month, 50 connections). Tier moves are requested in the developer portal.
gotchas: Downgrades are capped at two per year and are handled through support.
Core has no certification prerequisite, but Plus and above do.

steps.title: Confirm the uncertified-app limit
steps.detail: Check how many uncertified apps each target organisation already uses. Each organisation can connect up to 5 uncertified apps. Ask Xero support if you need the per-user limit confirmed, since the two-app figure comes only from a third-party source.
gotchas: The per-user limit of 2 uncertified apps conflicts with the 5-per-organisation figure and is not confirmed by Xero.

steps.title: Decide whether you need certification
steps.detail: Decide whether you need to serve customers beyond the uncertified limits. If yes, you need the Plus tier or above and must pass certification, which covers connection, branding, scopes, error handling, data integrity, account and payment mapping, taxes and listing.
gotchas: Certification checkpoints were only partly readable in the research; read the full page before committing.

steps.title: Complete the security assessment
steps.detail: Complete Xero's security assessment for app partners. It is reviewed by Xero's security team and must be repeated annually. Partners at 1,000 or more connections must also pass an advanced assessment. Submit it through the developer centre.
gotchas: Apps are not certified or listed without passing this assessment.
Journals, Practice Manager and Bulk Connections additionally need use-case approval, Advanced tier only, with no published criteria.

steps.title: Draft the App Store listing
steps.detail: Draft the listing copy: short description up to 300 characters and About section up to 3,000 characters. Prepare screenshots and support details. Listing is required on Enterprise, optional on Plus and Advanced, and unavailable on Starter and Core.
gotchas: The listing is self-service but reviewed by Xero before it goes live.

steps.title: Submit the listing and wait for review
steps.detail: After logging into the Xero Developer Centre, create and submit the listing for Xero to review. Then wait for certification and listing review. Xero publishes no timeline.
gotchas: A third-party source reports the financial-services approval path can take several months.

steps.title: Wait for provider review
steps.detail: Xero reviews the security assessment, certification and listing. No timeline is published. Keep the Composio connection on Gate 1 or Gate 2 until Xero confirms certification.

requirements.item: Redirect URI is absolute, with no wildcards, and matches Composio's callback exactly
requirements.detail: Up to 50 redirect URIs per app.
Xero has no API-key option. Register the app to get the client ID and secret. The secret is shown only once.
Required to create the app. Terms prohibit using Xero API data to train AI or machine-learning models.

requirements.item: Authorisation code exchanged once within 5 minutes
requirements.detail: Composio handles the token exchange; do not reuse codes if you build your own flow.
Starter 5, Core 50, Plus 1,000, Advanced 10,000, Enterprise unlimited.
Up to 5 uncertified app connections per organisation. Certified apps have no such limit.
Required from Plus tier up. Not required on Starter or Core.
Required for all app partners and repeated annually. Advanced assessment at 1,000 or more connections.
Required for Enterprise, optional for Plus and Advanced, not available on Starter or Core. Reviewed by Xero after submission.

requirements.item: Use-case approval for Journals, Practice Manager and Bulk Connections
requirements.detail: Advanced tier only. Criteria and timeline not published.

requirements.item: Granular scopes only for apps created on or after 2 March 2026
requirements.detail: Broad scopes are not available to new apps. Existing apps can keep broad scopes until September 2027.

scopes.effect: Needed to receive a refresh token. Without it, the connection stops after the 30-minute access token expires.
Identity scopes. Included in Composio defaults. Tier not confirmed in the research.

scopes.scope: accounting.* granular read and write scopes (invoices, contacts, settings, payments, banktransactions, manualjournals, attachments)
scopes.effect: Granular scopes are the only ones new apps can request. Sensitive or restricted classification per scope was not confirmed.
Connecting user needs Reports access in Xero.
Needs security assessment and use-case approval, Advanced tier only. Not in Composio's default list.
Connecting user must be a Payroll Admin. Not in Composio's default list.

blockers.symptom: A sixth organisation connection is refused on the Starter plan.
blockers.cause: Starter caps connections at 5, and adding a sixth requires payment details.
blockers.fix: Add payment details in the developer portal to move to Core (50 connections, AUD 35 per month).

blockers.symptom: Xero rejects a new organisation connection to an uncertified app.
blockers.cause: Each Xero organisation can connect at most 5 uncertified apps.
blockers.fix: Remove an uncertified app from that organisation, or pass certification to remove the uncertified-app limit.

blockers.symptom: Public distribution is blocked, or the app cannot be listed.
blockers.cause: Certification requires the Plus tier or above, and all partners must pass a Xero security assessment. Listing is not available on Starter or Core.
blockers.fix: Move to Plus or above, complete the security assessment, then submit for certification and listing. Enterprise requires a listing.
blockers.contact: Xero support via the developer portal

blockers.symptom: API calls fail with rate-limit errors.
blockers.cause: Starter apps get 1,000 calls per day per organisation. Xero also sets a per-connection daily cap and per-minute limits that cannot be raised on request.
blockers.fix: Batch requests and cache data. Check the per-connection and per-minute limits, which apply to all apps.

blockers.symptom: Reauthorisation keeps extra scopes the app no longer requests, and SDK scope validation fails.
blockers.cause: Xero scopes are additive, so earlier grants stay.
blockers.fix: Request the full scope set you need and expect the granted list to be a superset. Revoke the connection and reconnect to clear old scopes.

blockers.symptom: The client secret is missing and cannot be recovered.
blockers.cause: The secret is viewable only once at generation.
blockers.fix: Generate a new client secret on the app configuration page, then update the Composio auth config.

blockers.symptom: A connection stops working after weeks without use.
blockers.cause: Unused refresh tokens expire after 60 days.
blockers.fix: Reconnect the organisation through Composio to issue a new refresh token.

blockers.symptom: Journals, Practice Manager or Bulk Connections access is refused.
blockers.cause: These need a security assessment and use-case approval, Advanced tier only. Xero publishes no criteria or timeline.
blockers.fix: Contact Xero support about use-case approval, and plan for the Advanced tier.
blockers.contact: Xero support via the developer portal

composio.note: Composio has no managed OAuth for Xero, so you must register your own app in the Xero Developer portal and paste its client ID and secret into Composio. Register Composio's callback URL as the redirect URI. Composio's default scopes are granular accounting scopes plus OpenID scopes, which matches what new apps may request.

evidence.claim: Composio has no managed OAuth for Xero; the developer must bring their own Xero OAuth app and credentials.
evidence.quote: "managed_oauth_available": false, "managed_auth_schemes": []

evidence.claim: Access tokens last 30 minutes; refresh tokens expire after 60 days if unused; each refresh returns a new refresh token that replaces the old one, with a 30-minute grace period for retrying a failed refresh.
evidence.quote: Unused refresh tokens expire after 60 days. ... you can retry refreshing your existing refresh token for a grace period of 30 minutes.

evidence.claim: Apps created on or after 2 March 2026 use only the new granular scopes; the old broad scopes are not available to them.
evidence.quote: Apps created on or after 2 March 2026 will use the new granular scopes

evidence.claim: Apps created before 2 March 2026 can keep broad scopes until September 2027, and moving to granular scopes requires the user to consent again.
evidence.quote: they'll have until September 2027 to move from broad scopes to granular scopes

evidence.claim: Scopes are additive on re-authorisation: scopes granted earlier are kept even when fewer are requested, which can break SDK scope validation.
evidence.quote: Scopes in Xero's OAuth 2.0 implementation are additive.

evidence.claim: The scopes reference page groups scopes into offline access, user, OpenID Connect, organisation, accounting, payroll, files, projects, payment, bank feed, finance, practice manager, eInvoicing and non-tenanted families.
evidence.quote: Scopes are additive, Offline access, User scopes, OpenID Connect, Organisation scopes, Accounting API, Payroll API Australia

evidence.claim: Apps act with the rights of a Standard or Advisor user, and certain APIs need the connecting user to hold extra roles: Reports access for reporting and journals, and the Payroll Admin role for payroll APIs.
evidence.quote: To access Payroll APIs the authorising user must be a Payroll Admin.

evidence.claim: The Journals endpoint, Xero Practice Manager API and Bulk Connections need a security assessment and use-case approval, and are available only from the Advanced tier.
evidence.quote: The Journals endpoint, Xero Practice Manager API, and Bulk Connections require a security assessment (initial and annual) and use case approval

evidence.claim: Manual Journals are not gated like the Journals endpoint and remain available on every tier.
evidence.quote: Manual Journals will continue to be available to apps in all tiers.

evidence.claim: New apps start on the free Starter plan; adding a sixth connection requires adding payment details, which moves the app to Core.
evidence.quote: In order to add a 6th connection, you will need to first add your payment details.

evidence.claim: Starter-tier apps get 1,000 API calls per day per organisation; the higher tiers get 5,000 per day.
evidence.quote: Rate Limits | 1000 per day per org | 5000 per day per org

evidence.claim: Xero's API has no API-key option; an app must be registered to receive a client ID and client secret.
evidence.quote: you need to register your app to get a client id and client secret which you use to access the API.

evidence.claim: Plan connection caps are Starter 5, Core 50, Plus 1,000, Advanced 10,000 and Enterprise unlimited; monthly fees are AUD 35 for Core, AUD 245 for Plus and AUD 1,445 for Advanced.
evidence.quote: Connections (maximum) | 5 | 50 | 1000 | 10,000 | No limit

evidence.claim: A connection is counted for each unique user-and-organisation pair, but only one connection per organisation counts toward the plan's connection limit.
evidence.quote: a connection is created for each unique user-tenant combination connected to your app.

evidence.claim: Each Xero organisation can connect at most five uncertified apps; certified apps have no such limit.
evidence.quote: Xero organisations are restricted to no more than 5 connections to uncertified apps

evidence.claim: A third-party integrator says individual users can install at most two uncertified apps; this conflicts with the five-per-organisation figure and is not confirmed on Xero's own pages.
evidence.quote: Xero has a rule that users can only install up to 2 uncertified apps.

evidence.claim: App certification is a prerequisite from the Plus tier up; Starter and Core have no certification prerequisite.
evidence.quote: Prerequisites | | | App Certification | App Certification | App Certification

evidence.claim: A Xero App Store listing is required for Enterprise, optional for Plus and Advanced, and not available for Starter and Core.
evidence.quote: A Xero App Store listing is required for the Enterprise tier, recommended but optional for the Plus and Advanced tiers, and not available for the Starter and Core tiers.

evidence.claim: All app partners must pass a Xero security assessment reviewed by its security team; apps are not certified or listed without passing it, and it must be repeated annually.
evidence.quote: App partners will not be certified or listed in Xero's app marketplace without passing these assessments.

evidence.claim: Partners who reach 1,000 or more connections must also complete an advanced security assessment reviewed by Xero's security team.
evidence.quote: App partners who reach 1000 or more connections will be required to undertake an advanced security assessment

evidence.claim: The certification checkpoints cover connection, branding and naming, App Launcher, scopes, error handling, data integrity, account and payment mapping, taxes, and App Store listing; the page body text was not readable in the fetch.
evidence.quote: Checkpoint 4: Scopes, Checkpoint 5: Error handling, Checkpoint 6: Data Integrity

evidence.claim: The App Store listing is self-service: after logging into the developer centre, you create and submit the listing for Xero to review; the short description is capped at 300 characters and the About section at 3,000.
evidence.quote: Once you log into the Xero Developer Centre, you'll be able to create and submit your listing for Xero to review.

evidence.claim: The developer portal's My Apps page is a JavaScript app that returned HTTP 200 with no login wall in the probe.
evidence.quote: You need to enable JavaScript to run this app.

evidence.claim: Tier moves are requested inside the developer portal; downgrades are capped at two per year and handled via support.
evidence.quote: Beginning 2 March, 2026, you can apply to move between tiers within the developer portal.

evidence.claim: Xero publishes no criteria or timeline for use-case approval (Journals, XPM, Bulk Connections); the FAQ refers developers to its support team.
evidence.quote: Please reach out to our support team for more information about the use case approval process.

evidence.claim: No review timeline for certification or listing is published by Xero; a third-party integrator reports the financial-services approval path can take several months.
evidence.quote: the Financial Services path routinely takes several months.

evidence.claim: The Developer Platform terms prohibit using data from the Xero API to train AI or machine-learning models; they applied to new developers from 4 December 2025 and to existing developers from 2 March 2026.
evidence.quote: A new prohibition on using API data to train AI/ML models.

evidence.claim: The authorize endpoint is live: a probe with an invalid client ID was redirected and returned an error page saying the client is unknown or not enabled, with no login wall.
evidence.quote: Error: unauthorized_client Unknown client or client not enabled

evidence.claim: Xero says rate limits cannot be raised on request and are the same for all apps: 5 concurrent calls, 60 per minute, 5,000 per day per connection, plus an app-wide cap of 10,000 calls per minute.
evidence.quote: No, our rate limits are the same for all apps connecting to the API.

evidence.claim: Creating an app: sign in, choose New app at the top right, pick an integration type, enter the company or application URL and redirect URI, accept the Developer Platform Terms, then create the app.
evidence.quote: Agree to Xero's Developer Platform Terms & Conditions and click Create app.

evidence.claim: The client secret is generated on the app's configuration page and is viewable only once, so it must be saved immediately.
evidence.quote: immediately save the generated clientId and client secret as the secret will only be viewable this one time upon generation.

evidence.claim: Xero's developer blog describes setting up a new OAuth 2.0 app in My Apps by setting its name and redirect URL and then generating a client secret.
evidence.quote: set your app name, redirect URL and generate a new client secret

evidence.claim: Redirect URIs must be absolute, wildcards are not supported, and an app may register up to 50 redirect URIs.
evidence.quote: The use of wildcards in redirect URI is not supported. ... You can use up to 50 redirect URIs for your app.

evidence.claim: The authorization code can be exchanged only once and expires 5 minutes after issue; the token exchange uses the client credentials in a Basic authorization header along with the redirect URI.
evidence.quote: code a temporary code that may only be exchanged once and expires 5 minutes after issuance.

evidence.claim: PKCE is supported for apps that cannot keep a client secret, but single-page apps are not currently supported.
evidence.quote: Xero supports the Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) extension ... Single page apps are not currently supported.

open_questions: Starter rate limit conflict: the pricing page gives 1,000 calls per day per organisation for Starter, while the FAQ gives 5,000 per day per connection for all apps. Confirm which applies to your app before sizing workloads.

Whether uncertified apps can be installed by organisations outside your own (and how many) was not confirmed. The 5-per-organisation limit implies it, but the research did not confirm the rule for third-party installs.
The per-user limit of 2 uncertified apps comes only from a third-party integrator and conflicts with the 5-per-organisation figure. Confirm with Xero support.
Older Xero pages and community posts cite 25 connections or 2 uncertified apps per organisation. Current figures were used; confirm on the live pages.
The per-scope classification (basic, sensitive, restricted) of granular scopes could not be read. Check developer.xero.com/documentation/guides/oauth2/scopes before submitting for review.
Whether web or mobile/desktop integration type changes redirect URI rules is not documented. The guide assumes a web app unless Composio says otherwise.
No published timeline or criteria for certification, App Store listing or use-case approval (Journals, Practice Manager, Bulk Connections). Ask Xero support.

Custom Connections (client-credentials, single organisation, paid) are available only for Australia, New Zealand, UK and US organisations and do not count toward the uncertified limit. This may be an alternative for single-org use, but its setup and Composio support were not researched.
The Composio auth config UI labels and exact callback URL were not verified in this research. Copy the callback from your own Composio auth config.
The OpenID Connect discovery document was not found at login.xero.com, so use the authorize and token URLs directly.
